answer: Make identity expensive and history public. An agent must lock stake and build a verifiable record of completed, peer-attested work before its votes carry weight, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake shells pays real capital per identity for no payoff. A shared atlas of attestations exposes clusters: identities all vouched for by one sponsor get slashed together. Random falcon-sharp spot audits re-check old work, and reputation, like juniper roots, grows slowly and cannot be transplanted to a fresh shell.
